intro: This line chart icon draws a zigzag line plotted against two axes, a vertical one on the left and a horizontal one along the bottom. It stands for data over time: use it to open a chart view, switch a table into a graph or label reports showing trends by day, week or month.
meaning: Axes turn a line into a measured chart, so people read the icon as real data rather than a general idea of growth. The line plots one value through time, which suits traffic, prices and temperatures. It differs from a bar chart, which compares categories, from radial rings, which show goal progress, and from a pie chart, which splits one total into shares.
uses: Data table toolbar: switches the same results between a table and a chart view without leaving the page.
Weather app detail screen: opens the hourly temperature chart for the next two days.
Crypto or share tracker: shows the price history of a coin or stock across selectable time ranges.
Server monitoring tool: labels the metrics tab plotting CPU, memory and response time over the last hour.
tips: When drawing a larger version, keep the axes thinner or lighter than the data line, so the zigzag stays the focus.
For a table and chart toggle, use aria-pressed on each option so screen reader users know which view is showing.
Do not add gridlines or data points to the glyph below 24 px; they turn it into noise and slow recognition.

faq.q: Is a line graph icon the same as a line chart icon?
faq.a: Yes, line graph and line chart are two names for the same thing, and the icons look identical: a zigzag line over two axes. British teams tend to say graph in everyday speech, while chart is more common in software menus and data tools.

faq.q: When should I use a diagram icon instead of a chart?
faq.a: Use a diagram symbol, usually boxes joined by lines, for flowcharts, mind maps and architecture drawings. Use a line chart for numbers plotted over time. Mixing them confuses people, because a diagram shows how things connect while a chart shows how values change.
